T: Old woods, thick and quiet. Somewhere a woodpecker is working very hard.
H: A farmhouse, turnips drying on the sill.
The sill is a slab of grey glass from before. Nobody knows what it was for. It makes a very good sill.
d: You knock. From inside: "We're not buying! Unless it's turnips. Are you turnips?"
f: Rows and rows of turnips. Millbrook grows nothing else, and is very proud of it.
F: A fence, mended with twine, hope and more twine.
c: A candle in an iron lantern on a post, burning steadily. It feels like the Archive's candles.
Q: Three old statues, toppled face-down in the moss. You turn one over.
Its face has been worn smooth. So have the others. Whoever they were, someone wanted them forgotten.
>: The road back east, toward the Courier Road.
w: The village well. Far down in the dark, something catches the light and glints.
Too deep to reach. Someone nimbler might manage it.

objects.name: Jory
lines: Morning! Or afternoon. Out here it's mostly turnip o'clock.

answer: Millbrook. Six families, one well, and the best turnips in the world.
We're the only village the king doesn't bother with. We've got nothing he wants. Except turnips. He doesn't want those either.
The king's soldiers came through last spring and took every bit of iron. Pots, nails, my grandad's teeth.
Left the turnips. Said they were "too heavy to carry and too sad to eat". The cheek.
Turnips don't care who's king. You plant them, you tend them, they come up. Every year.
There's a lesson in that, my mum said. She never said what it was.

questions.ask: You smell like a turnip, Jory.
answer: Thank you. Took me years.
...Oh, you meant it rude. Well. The turnips heard that.

objects.name: Old Wenna
lines: Stop. You. Arm-wrestle me for directions.
No? Soft. You're not from the Kingdom, then. Good.

answer: East, past the old fort. They call it the Berserker Kingdom now.
In my great-grandmother's day it had another name. Pretty one. Nobody says it any more.
The fort in the hill's haunted. Soldiers from the old war, still drilling in the dark.
My nephew went in on a dare. Came out three days later, saluting everything. Still does. Salutes the cat.
Keeps the arms young. At my age you do one thing a day that's hard, or the days start doing it to you.
Ninety-one years and nothing's snapped yet. Sit down.
* She cracks her knuckles, one at a time. You decide you're not that lost.

lines: Heard you won in the pit. Five of the king's own, and the Warden.
Still soft. Less soft. Sit down. Arm.

objects.name: Madame Oriel
lines: Ah! I have foreseen you. You are... a tall man named Gerald.
No? Then the stars are having an off day. Cross my palm with a habit and I'll try again.

answer: I see... a door. You will open it. Then another door. Life is mostly doors.
Also a goose. Beware the goose. Or befriend it. The vision was unclear about the goose.
The king in the east has not aged a day in five hundred years. I have foreseen that this is odd.
That one I actually got right.
Once a year, exactly. I just never know which time it is.

questions.ask: Some seer. You can't even guess my name.
answer: I can, dear. I'm being polite.
You're a Gerald on the inside. It's the face that's wrong.

lines: You've met a tall man named Gerald.
Don't tell me. I know. Once a year, exactly, and this was the year.

objects.name: Professor Hoot
lines: Zzz... hm? Ah. A player. Don't mind me.
I'm resting my eyes. Have you rested yours? You've been looking at this little screen for a while.
BY ORDER OF THE KING: all iron to be surrendered at the border post. Turnips may be kept.
Behind the toppled statues, deep in the moss: a Heart Piece.
Someone hid it where the forgotten things are. Nobody looks there.
